def create_pipeline() -> Pipeline:
    """Return the corpus_ingest pipeline: two source branches → merge → select.

    DAG shape::

        raw_ccnews_source  → snapshot_raw_ccnews  → normalize_ccnews  ─┐
                                                                         ├─ merge_documents → select_documents → documents
        raw_miracl_source  → snapshot_raw_miracl  → normalize_miracl  ─┘

    Why two branches:
        CC-News provides the bulk English corpus (~190k rows after language
        filter). MIRACL corpus provides the 7,921 unique passages referenced in
        the MIRACL en-dev qrels. Keeping them separate lets each source use its
        own ``CorpusSourceConfig`` (different column names, id prefixes, field
        maps) without any conditional logic inside the nodes.

    Fidelity guarantee:
        ``merge_documents`` places MIRACL passages after CC-News rows, so
        ``select_documents`` sees them before the ``max_documents`` cap is
        applied. Provided ``max_documents`` ≥ total MIRACL passages (~8k), every
        qrels-positive document survives into the primary layer.

    Catalog entries required (``conf/base/catalog.yml``):
        - ``raw_ccnews_source`` — :class:`HuggingFaceDataset` (streaming, filter en)
        - ``raw_ccnews`` — :class:`kedro_datasets.json.JSONDataset`
        - ``normalized_ccnews`` — :class:`kedro_datasets.json.JSONDataset`
        - ``raw_miracl_source`` — :class:`HfFileDataset` (JSONL.gz via HfFileSystem)
        - ``raw_miracl`` — :class:`kedro_datasets.json.JSONDataset`
        - ``normalized_miracl`` — :class:`kedro_datasets.json.JSONDataset`

    Parameters required (``conf/base/parameters.yml``):
        - ``corpus_ccnews`` — :class:`CorpusSourceConfig` for CC-News
        - ``corpus_miracl`` — :class:`CorpusSourceConfig` for MIRACL corpus
        - ``corpus_selection`` — unchanged (language filter + max_documents cap)
    """
    return pipeline(
        [
            # ── CC-News branch ─────────────────────────────────────────────
            node(
                func=snapshot_raw_corpus,
                inputs="raw_ccnews_source",
                outputs="raw_ccnews",
                name="snapshot_raw_ccnews",
            ),
            node(
                func=normalize_corpus,
                inputs=["raw_ccnews", "params:corpus_ccnews"],
                outputs="normalized_ccnews",
                name="normalize_ccnews",
            ),
            # ── MIRACL corpus branch ────────────────────────────────────────
            node(
                func=snapshot_raw_corpus,
                inputs="raw_miracl_source",
                outputs="raw_miracl",
                name="snapshot_raw_miracl",
            ),
            node(
                func=normalize_corpus,
                inputs=["raw_miracl", "params:corpus_miracl"],
                outputs="normalized_miracl",
                name="normalize_miracl",
            ),
            # ── Merge + select ──────────────────────────────────────────────
            node(
                func=merge_documents,
                inputs=["normalized_ccnews", "normalized_miracl"],
                outputs="merged_documents",
                name="merge_documents",
            ),
            node(
                func=select_documents,
                inputs=["merged_documents", "params:corpus_selection"],
                outputs="documents",
                name="select_documents",
            ),
        ]
    )

# Data catalog — the single place that knows where data lives.
#
# Every corpus and index path in the project is declared here rather than opened
# inside a node, so `kedro viz` renders true lineage and swapping a local corpus
# for a Hugging Face one is a config change (`--env prod`), not a code change.
#
# Layers follow the Kedro convention:
#   01_raw          verbatim source rows, exactly as fetched
#   02_intermediate mapped onto the Document schema
#   03_primary      filtered and capped: the corpus a build actually consumes
#   08_reporting    evaluation output
#
# `${runtime_params:name,default}` lets the Typer CLI keep its --input / --index
# flags: those flags are forwarded as Kedro runtime params and resolve here.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 01_raw — acquisition                                                #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Default source is a local file so `kedro run --pipeline corpus_ingest` never
# touches the network unless the prod environment overrides it.
raw_corpus_source:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:raw_source_path,data/01_raw/corpus_source.jsonl}

raw_corpus:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/01_raw/corpus_snapshot.jsonl

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 02_intermediate — normalised to the Document schema                 #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

normalized_documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/02_intermediate/documents.jsonl

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 03_primary — the build-ready corpus                                 #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

# corpus_ingest WRITES this and index_build reads it, so its default must be a
# generated path. It must never default into data/sample/: that directory holds a
# committed fixture, and an acquisition run would overwrite it.
# Sample builds reach the fixture by passing it explicitly —
# `cybernaut-mini build --input data/sample/documents.jsonl` — which arrives here
# as the input_path runtime param.
documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:input_path,data/03_primary/corpus.jsonl}

judgments:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:judgments_path,data/sample/judgments.jsonl}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# The index                                                           #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

# One catalog entry for the whole index directory. `save` performs the canonical
# write (`_VALID` last); `load` returns a query-ready LoadedIndex, which is how
# the evaluation pipeline consumes it.
shard_index:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.ShardIndexDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:index_path,artifacts/sample}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 08_reporting                                                        #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

eval_report:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.CanonicalJsonDataset
  filepath: data/08_reporting/eval_report.json

# Kedro-side defaults. The Typer CLI passes the chosen configs/*.yaml as extra_params,
# which override these at run time.
#
# Paths are NOT parameters any more — they live in conf/base/catalog.yml and are
# overridden per run via `${runtime_params:...}` (the CLI's --input / --index flags)
# or per environment via `--env prod`.
#
# These defaults MUST mirror the EmbeddingConfig defaults in src/cybernaut_mini/
# config.py. The two are read by different entrypoints — `kedro run` reads this file,
# while the Typer CLI calls load_config() and gets the dataclass defaults — so if they
# drift, the same corpus builds a different index depending on how it was invoked.
#
# They deliberately do NOT mirror configs/default.yaml: that file is the quality
# profile and selects sentence_transformers, which lives behind the optional 'st'
# extra. A bare `kedro run` must work on the default install.
seed: 42
embedding:
  # Static distilled embeddings: real semantic structure, no torch, core dependency.
  # Downloads weights on first use, so it is NOT offline-safe on a cold cache — use
  # provider 'hash' (configs/tiny.yaml, or --offline) for that.
  #
  # Not 'hash' by default because shards are k-means clusters over these vectors:
  # feature hashing has no semantics to cluster on, which makes shard selection
  # (blog stage 5) look broken when the real fault is the embedder.
  provider: model2vec
  # Empty resolves to the provider's default in PROVIDER_DEFAULT_MODEL
  # (minishlab/potion-multilingual-128M for model2vec).
  model: ""
  # Commit SHA of the model weights. null resolves to the repo's default branch,
  # which is fine locally but not reproducible: two builds months apart can embed
  # with different tensors and silently yield a different index from one corpus.
  # Production builds must pin it — see conf/prod/parameters.yml.
  revision: null

  # report their own dimension from the loaded weights and ignore this.
  dim: 256
index:
  n_shards: 12
  max_keywords: 30
  max_entities: 30
  cooccurrence_window: 5
  min_edge_count: 2
rrf:
  k: 60
  dense_weight: 1.0
  lexical_weight: 1.0
  entity_weight: 0.5
agent:
  exploration_constant: 1.2
  max_expansions: 5
  max_retrieval_calls: 18
  judge: heuristic
  query_generator: heuristic

# How many shards the router is allowed to select per query when computing
# shard_recall@N. Matches DEFAULT_CANDIDATE_DEPTH in query.s5_select (100)
# so the metric measures the width the system actually runs with.
shard_beam_n: 100

corpus_selection:
  languages: null
  metadata_equals: null

# Set by the CLI (or `kedro run --params offline=true`) per invocation.
offline: false

# Data catalog — the single place that knows where data lives.
#
# Every corpus and index path in the project is declared here rather than opened
# inside a node, so `kedro viz` renders true lineage and swapping a local corpus
# for a Hugging Face one is a config change (`--env prod`), not a code change.
#
# Layers follow the Kedro convention:
#   01_raw          verbatim source rows, exactly as fetched
#   02_intermediate mapped onto the Document schema
#   03_primary      filtered and capped: the corpus a build actually consumes
#   08_reporting    evaluation output
#
# `${runtime_params:name,default}` lets the Typer CLI keep its --input / --index
# flags: those flags are forwarded as Kedro runtime params and resolve here.

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 01_raw — acquisition                                                #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

# Default source is a local file so `kedro run --pipeline corpus_ingest` never
# touches the network unless the prod environment overrides it.
raw_corpus_source:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:raw_source_path,data/01_raw/corpus_source.jsonl}

raw_corpus:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/01_raw/corpus_snapshot.jsonl

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 02_intermediate — normalised to the Document schema                 #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

normalized_documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: data/02_intermediate/documents.jsonl

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 03_primary — the build-ready corpus                                 #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

# corpus_ingest WRITES this and index_build reads it, so its default must be a
# generated path. It must never default into data/sample/: that directory holds a
# committed fixture, and an acquisition run would overwrite it.
# Sample builds reach the fixture by passing it explicitly —
# `cybernaut-mini build --input data/sample/documents.jsonl` — which arrives here
# as the input_path runtime param.
documents:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:input_path,data/03_primary/corpus.jsonl}

judgments:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.JsonlDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:judgments_path,data/sample/judgments.jsonl}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# The index                                                           #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

# One catalog entry for the whole index directory. `save` performs the canonical
# write (`_VALID` last); `load` returns a query-ready LoadedIndex, which is how
# the evaluation pipeline consumes it.
shard_index:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.ShardIndexDataset
  filepath: ${runtime_params:index_path,artifacts/sample}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #
# 08_reporting                                                        #
# ------------------------------------------------------------------ #

eval_report:
  type: cybernaut_mini.datasets.CanonicalJsonDataset
  filepath: data/08_reporting/eval_report.json

Suggested grouping: (1) query pipeline s1-s8 + stage tests (src/cybernaut_mini/query/, tests/test_s*.py); (2) storage.py, shard_artifacts.py, accel.py + their tests + scripts/with-accel.sh; (3) config/models/embeddings/retrieval/routing/expansion/indexing refactor + affected tests + uv.lock + pyproject.toml; (4) scripts (setup_mac.sh, preso.sh, check, sync_env.py), devcontainer-adjacent files, ONBOARDING.md, README.md, Makefile, .env.example, conf changes. Inspect `git status --short` and `git diff --stat` first and adjust grouping so each commit is self-contained (tests that belong with code go in the same commit). Run `uv run pytest -q` BEFORE committing to confirm green (fastText cache is warm; suite takes ~80s). """corpus_ingest pipeline definition.

Acquisition is a separate pipeline from ``index_build`` on purpose: fetching a
corpus is a slow, networked, rate-limited step that should run once, while an index
gets rebuilt many times over the same snapshot as configuration is tuned.

Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — supplies the
    "Documents" node at the head of the build-time flow. Local copy:
    ``data/00_reference/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.

Assumptions:
    - Acquisition and build have different cadences. Splitting them means a config
      sweep costs zero network calls.
    - ``corpus_ingest + index_build`` composes into the ``production`` pipeline, so
      the split costs nothing when a single end-to-end run is what you want.

Alternatives considered:
    - One pipeline with fetch as its first node: a single command, no composition
      needed. Rejected because every index rebuild would then re-hit the Hub, which
      is slow, rate-limited, and pointless when the snapshot has not changed.
    - A standalone ``scripts/fetch_corpus.py``: the smallest possible change.
      Rejected because it puts acquisition outside the catalog, which is exactly the
      arrangement this pipeline exists to remove — no lineage, no environment
      switching, no versioning.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from kedro.pipeline import Pipeline, node, pipeline

from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.corpus_ingest.nodes import (
    build_miracl_judgments,
    merge_documents,
    normalize_corpus,
    select_documents,
    snapshot_raw_corpus,
    validate_judgments,
)


def create_judgment_pipeline() -> Pipeline:
    """Return the judgment_ingest pipeline: MIRACL source → judgments.

    Runs independently of ``corpus_ingest``. The ``validate_judgments`` node
    depends on ``documents`` (produced by the corpus branch), so it must run
    after that branch completes. In practice: run ``judgment_ingest`` only when
    ``documents`` already exists (post corpus_ingest), or as part of ``production``
    where Kedro resolves the dependency automatically.
    """
    return pipeline(
        [
            node(
                func=build_miracl_judgments,
                inputs="miracl_en_dev_source",
                outputs="miracl_judgments_unvalidated",
                name="build_miracl_judgments",
            ),
            node(
                func=validate_judgments,
                inputs=["miracl_judgments_unvalidated", "documents"],
                outputs="judgments",
                name="validate_judgments",
            ),
        ]
    )


def create_pipeline() -> Pipeline:
    """Return the corpus_ingest pipeline: two source branches → merge → select.

    DAG shape::

        raw_ccnews_source  → snapshot_raw_ccnews  → normalize_ccnews  ─┐
                                                                         ├─ merge_documents → select_documents → documents
        raw_miracl_source  → snapshot_raw_miracl  → normalize_miracl  ─┘

    Why two branches:
        CC-News provides the bulk English corpus (~190k rows after language
        filter). MIRACL corpus provides the 7,921 unique passages referenced in
        the MIRACL en-dev qrels. Keeping them separate lets each source use its
        own ``CorpusSourceConfig`` (different column names, id prefixes, field
        maps) without any conditional logic inside the nodes.

    Fidelity guarantee:
        ``merge_documents`` places MIRACL passages after CC-News rows, so
        ``select_documents`` sees them before the ``max_documents`` cap is
        applied. Provided ``max_documents`` ≥ total MIRACL passages (~8k), every
        qrels-positive document survives into the primary layer.

    Catalog entries required (``conf/base/catalog.yml``):
        - ``raw_ccnews_source`` — :class:`HuggingFaceDataset` (streaming, filter en)
        - ``raw_ccnews`` — :class:`kedro_datasets.json.JSONDataset`
        - ``normalized_ccnews`` — :class:`kedro_datasets.json.JSONDataset`
        - ``raw_miracl_source`` — :class:`HfFileDataset` (JSONL.gz via HfFileSystem)
        - ``raw_miracl`` — :class:`kedro_datasets.json.JSONDataset`
        - ``normalized_miracl`` — :class:`kedro_datasets.json.JSONDataset`

    Parameters required (``conf/base/parameters.yml``):
        - ``corpus_ccnews`` — :class:`CorpusSourceConfig` for CC-News
        - ``corpus_miracl`` — :class:`CorpusSourceConfig` for MIRACL corpus
        - ``corpus_selection`` — unchanged (language filter + max_documents cap)
    """
    return pipeline(
        [
            # ── CC-News branch ─────────────────────────────────────────────
            node(
                func=snapshot_raw_corpus,
                inputs="raw_ccnews_source",
                outputs="raw_ccnews",
                name="snapshot_raw_ccnews",
            ),
            node(
                func=normalize_corpus,
                inputs=["raw_ccnews", "params:corpus_ccnews"],
                outputs="normalized_ccnews",
                name="normalize_ccnews",
            ),
            # ── MIRACL corpus branch ────────────────────────────────────────
            node(
                func=snapshot_raw_corpus,
                inputs="raw_miracl_source",
                outputs="raw_miracl",
                name="snapshot_raw_miracl",
            ),
            node(
                func=normalize_corpus,
                inputs=["raw_miracl", "params:corpus_miracl"],
                outputs="normalized_miracl",
                name="normalize_miracl",
            ),
            # ── Merge + select ──────────────────────────────────────────────
            node(
                func=merge_documents,
                inputs=["normalized_ccnews", "normalized_miracl"],
                outputs="merged_documents",
                name="merge_documents",
            ),
            node(
                func=select_documents,
                inputs=["merged_documents", "params:corpus_selection"],
                outputs="documents",
                name="select_documents",
            ),
        ]
    )

content.subject: M1.4: MIRACL qrels → Judgment loader + tests
content.description: Build the MIRACL en dev topics+qrels → Judgment loader per Phase 1.4 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md. Read .omc/research/m1-discovery.md FIRST for exact repo/config/column names and SHAs (task #2 produces it). Implementation: a pure normalization function (new module src/cybernaut_mini/pipelines/corpus_ingest/ or src/cybernaut_mini/corpus.py — follow where CorpusSourceConfig lives) mapping topic rows + qrels rows onto Judgment {query_id, question, relevant_document_ids: dict[str,int]} (src/cybernaut_mini/models.py:255), with docids prefixed to match the corpus id_prefix scheme ('mir') so judgment docids align with Document ids built by the ingest. Grades preserved (MIRACL is binary 0/1 — keep the int). Kedro wiring: catalog entries for the raw topics/qrels sources (HuggingFaceDataset, pinned SHAs from discovery doc) and an output JsonlDataset at data/03_primary/miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl in conf/prod/catalog.yml — coordinate with task #7 (prod conf rewrite) via team-lead if you both touch conf/prod at the same time; prefer putting ONLY the judgments entries in and messaging the lead. Every judgment docid must resolve against the corpus — add a validation guard that raises listing missing docids. Unit tests with in-memory rows (no network): mapping, prefixing, grade preservation, empty-qrels raise. Run `uv run pytest -q` + `uv run ruff check .` before completing.

content.subject: M1.3: multi-source corpus_ingest (ccnews + miracl branches + merge)
content.description: Extend corpus_ingest to two sources per Phase 1.3 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md. Read .omc/research/m1-discovery.md FIRST (task #2 output) for field maps. Current pipeline: snapshot_raw_corpus → normalize_corpus → select_documents (src/cybernaut_mini/pipelines/corpus_ingest/nodes.py, pipeline.py). Add a second source branch: catalog inputs raw_corpus_source (ccnews) and raw_corpus_source_miracl, each with its own snapshot + normalize (per-source CorpusSourceConfig from parameters: id_prefix 'ccn' / 'mir' so ids cannot collide), then a new pure `merge_documents` node (dedupe by id — raise on collision, deterministic order: sort by id) feeding the existing select_documents. Keep nodes pure (no I/O — sources come from the catalog, per the module docstring at nodes.py:1-27). Corpus composition rule from the plan: the miracl branch must NOT be capped (all qrels-referenced docs stay in); the ccnews branch takes the max_rows/max_documents cap so total lands ≈200k. Parameterize per-source selection in conf/base/parameters.yml (base keeps null/off defaults so the fixture path still works single-source; document that). Update conf/base/catalog.yml with the new intermediate entries (miracl paths). Unit tests for merge (collision raise, ordering, empty-branch raise) in tests/test_build.py style. Run `uv run pytest -q` + `uv run ruff check .` + `uv run mypy src` before completing. Follow the learning-first docstring convention (blog ref, assumptions, alternatives rejected).

content.subject: M1.6: prod conf rewrite — CC-News + MIRACL sources, 256 shards
content.description: Rewrite conf/prod per Phase 1.6 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md, replacing the NOSIBLE/prediction source (ruled out by scope Amendment #6). Read .omc/research/m1-discovery.md for pinned SHAs and column lists (task #2), and the multi-source catalog shape from task #6's changes to conf/base/catalog.yml. conf/prod/catalog.yml: raw_corpus_source → stanford-oval/ccnews (HuggingFaceDataset, pinned SHA, streaming: true, max_rows sized so post-normalization ccnews docs + miracl docs ≈ 200k — use discovery doc numbers), raw_corpus_source_miracl → miracl corpus source filtered to qrels-referenced docs (coordinate with how task #6 implemented the miracl branch; the qrels docid filter may need a dedicated dataset param or node — follow what #6 built), artifact paths prefixed ccnews_miracl_ (raw/intermediate/primary/artifacts/ccnews-miracl-200k). Keep the judgments entries task #5 adds — merge, don't clobber; message team-lead if you hit a conflict. conf/prod/parameters.yml: per-source corpus field_maps from the discovery doc (ccnews id_prefix 'ccn', miracl 'mir', min_text_chars per discovery recommendation), corpus_selection.languages [en], index.n_shards 256 with an updated rationale comment (200k docs / 256 shards ≈ 780 docs/shard — between the 390 the old comment argued and the scope target's 1000), embedding block unchanged (e5-small pinned revision stays). content.subject: M1.7-1.9: real fixture slice, retire data/sample, attribution + licence
content.description: Per Phases 1.7-1.9 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md. Using the streaming loader (task #3) and qrels loader (task #5): (1) Pull a small REAL fixture slice — all docs referenced by ~25 MIRACL en dev queries (every qrels positive included) plus ~200 CC-News en docs (< 250 CC-News docs total for licensing) — and commit it to data/01_raw/fixtures/ as documents.jsonl + judgments.jsonl in canonical Document/Judgment form, with a small script or documented command showing how it was produced (reproducible: pinned SHAs from .omc/research/m1-discovery.md). (2) Repoint everything that used data/sample: configs/tiny.yaml, Makefile build-sample/search-sample/eval-sample targets → build-fixture/search-fixture/eval-fixture (Makefile:17-32), tests/conftest.py and any test reading data/sample (rg 'data/sample' to find them). Keep the offline hash-provider path working for tests (configs/tiny.yaml stays offline-safe). (3) Write data/ATTRIBUTION.md + data/LICENSE-DATA: CC-News (per-article publisher copyright, Common Crawl ToU, cite stanford-oval/ccnews + SHA), MIRACL (Apache-2.0 + SHA). (4) Delete data/sample/ and scripts/generate_sample_corpus.py; acceptance: `rg -l "data/sample|generate_sample_corpus"` has no hits in src/, tests/, conf/, configs/, Makefile, scripts/. content.subject: M4.2-4.4: calibration + 200k build + eval + baseline doc
content.description: Per Phase 2.2-2.4 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md. All M1 tasks and shard_recall@N (#4) must be complete. (1) Calibration: run the production pipeline with max_rows≈20k (`scripts/with-accel.sh uv run kedro run --env prod --pipeline production --params ...` or a temporary max_rows override — do NOT edit the committed conf for this), record wall-clock; extrapolate to 200k and report the estimate to team-lead BEFORE starting the full run (lead decides go/no-go if extrapolation exceeds ~4h). (2) Full run: 200k docs / 256 shards with `scripts/with-accel.sh` (MPS + thread tuning), then `uv run kedro run --env prod --pipeline evaluation`. Record wall-clock + peak RSS (e.g. /usr/bin/time -l). (3) Verify acceptance criteria 2-4 of the plan: 256 shards present, doc count in [190k, 200k], every judgment docid resolves in the index, eval_report.json has 4 modes × 5 metrics incl. shard_recall@N with no all-zero/NaN mode. (4) Write docs/baselines/ccnews-miracl-200k.md: per-mode metric table, corpus SHAs, embedder revision (conf/prod/parameters.yml), shard count, build wall-clock, machine description; label metrics as MIRACL benchmark metrics never to be merged with generated per-shard evals (scope Amendment #7). (5) Sanity gates: hybrid must not underperform BOTH lexical and dense; shard_recall@N must beat random-N baseline (compute random baseline as N/256 expected). On gate failure: report to team-lead with the numbers, do NOT tune. Commit the baseline doc + eval report.

class HfFileDataset(AbstractDataset[None, list[dict[str, Any]]]):
    """Read-only corpus source backed by JSONL.gz files on the Hugging Face Hub.

    For datasets whose ``load_dataset`` loading script is deprecated (e.g.
    ``miracl/miracl-corpus``), individual shard files are accessed directly via
    :class:`huggingface_hub.HfFileSystem` rather than the ``datasets`` library.
    The caller supplies a glob pattern relative to the repo root; matching shards
    are read in alphabetical order so the result is deterministic.

    Blog ref: https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1 — MIRACL corpus
        as the fidelity substrate for eval; every docid in the qrels must land in
        the built index. Local copy: ``docs/blog-archive/the-road-to-cybernaut-1.md``.

    Assumptions:
        - All files matched by ``path_pattern`` are JSONL compressed with gzip
          (``.jsonl.gz``). Mixed or uncompressed shards are not supported.
        - ``filter_column`` + ``filter_values`` are designed for docid-set filters
          (thousands of values, O(1) set lookup per row). Pass the full qrel docid
          set to guarantee the fidelity rule: every qrels-positive doc is in the
          raw snapshot, so recall is never artificially capped. When both are
          ``None`` the whole dataset streams through; ``max_rows`` caps it.
        - Row counting across shards follows shard alphabetical order. A partial
          last shard is consumed only to the cap — its remaining bytes are not
          downloaded.

    Alternatives rejected:
        - Extending :class:`HuggingFaceDataset` with a ``file_mode`` flag: the
          two loading paths (``load_dataset`` vs ``HfFileSystem + gzip``) import
          entirely different libraries and share zero logic. A flag would produce
          a class with two unrelated personalities. A dedicated class keeps each
          path independently followable.
        - ``hf_hub_download`` per shard (requires enumerating all shard names
          up front): ``HfFileSystem.glob`` lists the directory lazily without
          materialising every path, which is what streaming decompression needs.

    Requires the ``hf`` extra (``uv sync --extra hf``).
    """

    _MUTABLE_REFS = frozenset({"main", "master", "head", "refs/heads/main"})
    _PLACEHOLDER_REF = "replace_with_commit_sha"

    def __init__(
        self,
        repo_id: str,
        revision: str,
        path_pattern: str,
        max_rows: int | None = None,
        filter_column: str | None = None,
        filter_values: list[str] | None = None,
        token_env: str = "HF_TOKEN",
    ) -> None:
        normalized_ref = (revision or "").strip().lower()
        if normalized_ref == self._PLACEHOLDER_REF:
            msg = (
                f"HfFileDataset({repo_id!r}): revision is still the placeholder. "
                f"Resolve the real SHA and paste it into conf/prod/catalog.yml:\n"
                f"  uv run python -c \"from huggingface_hub import HfApi; "
                f"print(HfApi().dataset_info('{repo_id}').sha)\""
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        if not normalized_ref or normalized_ref in self._MUTABLE_REFS:
            msg = (
                f"HfFileDataset({repo_id!r}): revision must pin an immutable "
                f"commit SHA or tag, got {revision!r}."
            )
            raise DatasetError(msg)
        self._repo_id = repo_id
        self._revision = revision
        self._path_pattern = path_pattern
        self._max_rows = max_rows
        self._filter_column = filter_column
        # Convert to a set once so per-row lookup is O(1).
        self._filter_values: frozenset[str] | None = (
            frozenset(filter_values) if filter_values is not None else None
        )
        self._token_env = token_env

    def load(self) -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
        import gzip
        import json

markdown# 01 — Corpus ingest: how raw rows become a build-ready corpus Blog: [The Road to Cybernaut-1](https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1) — this notebook covers the **Documents** node at the head of the build-time flow, everything that happens *before* text processing and embedding. Nothing here opens a file path. Every read and write goes through the Kedro **catalog**, which is what makes the same pipeline work against the 63-document sample and a 100,000-row Hugging Face corpus without a code change. ```mermaid flowchart TB S[("raw_corpus_source
HuggingFaceDataset pinned to a SHA
· or a local JSONL")] S --> A["snapshot_raw_corpus"] A --> B[("raw_corpus
data/01_raw
source rows, verbatim")] B --> C["normalize_corpus
field_map → Document schema"] C --> D[("normalized_documents
data/02_intermediate
ids, titles, cleaned text")] D --> E["select_documents
language · metadata · cap"] E --> F[("documents
data/03_primary
what a build consumes")] F -.-> G["index_build pipeline"] ``` **What you will see calculated below** 1. What normalisation actually removes, row by row, and why. 2. That document ids do not depend on row order — the property the whole reproducibility story rests on. 3. How `min_text_chars` trades corpus size against document quality. markdown## Bootstrap `kedro jupyter lab` injects `catalog` automatically. This helper does the same thing from *any* kernel — plain Jupyter, VS Code, or the headless executor that runs this notebook in the test suite — so the file you are reading is the file CI verifies. from cybernaut_mini.notebook import kedro_catalog, project_root, run_pipeline print("project root:", project_root()) catalog = kedro_catalog() print("catalog entries:", sorted(catalog.keys())) markdown## A deliberately messy source Real corpora are not clean. This demo source mirrors the schema the NOSIBLE Hugging Face datasets publish (`text` / `label` / `netloc` / `url`) and plants one of each failure mode the normaliser has to survive. We write it through the catalog entry `raw_corpus_source`, exactly where a `HuggingFaceDataset` would sit in the `prod` environment. GOOD = ( "Analysts expect refinancing conditions to tighten materially over the coming " "quarter as corporate credit spreads widen." ) source_rows = [ # 4 ordinary rows, alternating labels so the metadata filter below has bite. {"text": f"{GOOD} Case {i}.", "label": "prediction" if i % 2 == 0 else "not-prediction", "netloc": "example.com", "url": f"https://example.com/a-{i}"} for i in range(4) ] + [ # Too short — below min_text_chars, dropped. {"text": "No comment.", "label": "not-prediction", "netloc": "example.com", "url": "https://example.com/short"}, # Duplicate url of a-0 — collapses to the first occurrence. {"text": f"{GOOD} A duplicate of the first row.", "label": "prediction", "netloc": "example.com", "url": "https://example.com/a-0"}, # Messy whitespace — kept, but normalised. {"text": "Ragged\n\n spacing and\ttabs throughout this otherwise fine passage body.", "label": "prediction", "netloc": "example.com", "url": "https://example.com/messy"}, # No url — still needs a stable id, derived from the body instead. {"text": f"{GOOD} This row has no url at all.", "label": "prediction", "netloc": "example.com", "url": ""}, ] catalog.save("raw_corpus_source", source_rows) print(f"wrote {len(source_rows)} source rows through the catalog") for row in source_rows: print(f" {len(row['text']):>4} chars url={row['url'] or '(none)':<32} {row['text'][:44]}...") markdown## Run the acquisition pipeline Three nodes, three catalog writes — one per layer. Acquisition is a *separate* pipeline from `index_build` on purpose: fetching is slow and rate-limited and should happen once, while an index gets rebuilt many times over the same snapshot as settings are tuned. run_pipeline( "corpus_ingest", corpus={ "field_map": {"text": "text", "url": "url"}, "metadata_fields": ["label", "netloc"], "default_language": "en", "id_prefix": "demo", "min_text_chars": 32, }, corpus_selection={"languages": None, "metadata_equals": None, "max_documents": None}, ) print("corpus_ingest complete") markdown## What each layer holds Now read all three layers back **through the catalog**. This is the payoff of the refactor: the layers are addressable by name, so you can inspect any stage without knowing where it lives on disk. raw = catalog.load("raw_corpus") normalized = catalog.load("normalized_documents") primary = catalog.load("documents") print(f"01_raw raw_corpus {len(raw):>3} rows (verbatim source)") print(f"02_intermediate normalized_documents {len(normalized):>3} docs (Document schema)") print(f"03_primary documents {len(primary):>3} docs (build-ready)") print() print(f"normalisation removed {len(raw) - len(normalized)} of {len(raw)} rows") markdown### Which rows were dropped, and why The normaliser skips unusable rows rather than raising on them. That is a deliberate choice: one malformed row out of 100,000 must not fail a multi-hour production build. Here we reconstruct the reason for each drop. from cybernaut_mini.corpus import CorpusSourceConfig, make_document_id config = CorpusSourceConfig( field_map={"text": "text", "url": "url"}, metadata_fields=["label", "netloc"], id_prefix="demo", min_text_chars=32, ) kept_ids = {doc["id"] for doc in normalized} seen: set[str] = set() print(f"{'verdict':<12} {'reason':<22} url") print("-" * 74) for row in raw: text = " ".join(row["text"].split()) natural_key = row["url"] or text doc_id = make_document_id(config.id_prefix, natural_key) if len(text) < config.min_text_chars: verdict, reason = "DROPPED", f"< {config.min_text_chars} chars" elif doc_id in seen: verdict, reason = "DROPPED", "duplicate natural key" else: verdict, reason = "kept", "" seen.add(doc_id) print(f"{verdict:<12} {reason:<22} {row['url'] or '(no url)'}") print() print(f"survivors: {len(kept_ids)}") markdown### Whitespace and derived titles These corpora ship passages with no title, but the shard manifest, the shard summary, and the `title\ntext` string that gets embedded all assume one exists. A title is therefore derived from the first sentence, cut on a word boundary. for doc in normalized: if "Ragged" in doc["text"]: print("raw text :", repr(next(r["text"] for r in raw if "Ragged" in r["text"]))) print("normalised:", repr(doc["text"])) print() print(f"{'id':<20} {'title':<62} chars") print("-" * 92) for doc in normalized: print(f"{doc['id']:<20} {doc['title'][:60]:<62} {len(doc['title']):>3}") markdown## Dynamic 1 — ids do not depend on row order This is the property everything else rests on. Ids are `blake2b` hashes of the row's natural key (its `url`, or the body text when there is none), **not** sequential counters. Re-fetching a corpus whose rows came back in a different order therefore produces the same ids, the same shard assignments, and the same byte-for-byte index. Sequential ids would renumber every document and silently invalidate every stored relevance judgment. import random from cybernaut_mini.corpus import normalize_rows forward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(source_rows, config)] shuffled = list(source_rows) random.Random(0).shuffle(shuffled) backward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(shuffled, config)] print("original order :", forward[:3], "...") print("shuffled order :", backward[:3], "...") print() print("identical:", forward == backward) assert forward == backward, "ids must not depend on row order" markdown## Dynamic 2 — `min_text_chars` trades size against quality The knob that decides how much of a public corpus survives. # 01 — Corpus ingest: how raw rows become a build-ready corpus Blog: [The Road to Cybernaut-1](https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1) — this notebook covers the **Documents** node at the head of the build-time flow, everything that happens *before* text processing and embedding. Nothing here opens a file path. Every read and write goes through the Kedro **catalog**, which is what makes the same pipeline work against the 63-document sample and a 100,000-row Hugging Face corpus without a code change. ```mermaid flowchart TB S[("raw_corpus_source
HuggingFaceDataset pinned to a SHA
· or a local JSONL")] S --> A["snapshot_raw_corpus"] A --> B[("raw_corpus
data/01_raw
source rows, verbatim")] B --> C["normalize_corpus
field_map → Document schema"] C --> D[("normalized_documents
data/02_intermediate
ids, titles, cleaned text")] D --> E["select_documents
language · metadata · cap"] E --> F[("documents
data/03_primary
what a build consumes")] F -.-> G["index_build pipeline"] ``` **What you will see calculated below** 1. What normalisation actually removes, row by row, and why. 2. That document ids do not depend on row order — the property the whole reproducibility story rests on. 3. How `min_text_chars` trades corpus size against document quality.

## Bootstrap

`kedro jupyter lab` injects `catalog` automatically. This helper does the same thing
from *any* kernel — plain Jupyter, VS Code, or the headless executor that runs this
notebook in the test suite — so the file you are reading is the file CI verifies.

from cybernaut_mini.notebook import kedro_catalog, project_root, run_pipeline

print("project root:", project_root())

catalog = kedro_catalog()
print("catalog entries:", sorted(catalog.keys()))

## A deliberately messy source

Real corpora are not clean. This demo source mirrors the schema the NOSIBLE
Hugging Face datasets publish (`text` / `label` / `netloc` / `url`) and plants one
of each failure mode the normaliser has to survive.

We write it through the catalog entry `raw_corpus_source`, exactly where a
`HuggingFaceDataset` would sit in the `prod` environment.

GOOD = (
    "Analysts expect refinancing conditions to tighten materially over the coming "
    "quarter as corporate credit spreads widen."
)

source_rows = [
    # 4 ordinary rows, alternating labels so the metadata filter below has bite.
    {"text": f"{GOOD} Case {i}.", "label": "prediction" if i % 2 == 0 else "not-prediction",
     "netloc": "example.com", "url": f"https://example.com/a-{i}"}
    for i in range(4)
] + [
    # Too short — below min_text_chars, dropped.
    {"text": "No comment.", "label": "not-prediction",
     "netloc": "example.com", "url": "https://example.com/short"},
    # Duplicate url of a-0 — collapses to the first occurrence.
    {"text": f"{GOOD} A duplicate of the first row.", "label": "prediction",
     "netloc": "example.com", "url": "https://example.com/a-0"},
    # Messy whitespace — kept, but normalised.
    {"text": "Ragged\n\n   spacing   and\ttabs throughout this otherwise fine passage body.",
     "label": "prediction", "netloc": "example.com", "url": "https://example.com/messy"},
    # No url — still needs a stable id, derived from the body instead.
    {"text": f"{GOOD} This row has no url at all.", "label": "prediction",
     "netloc": "example.com", "url": ""},
]

catalog.save("raw_corpus_source", source_rows)
print(f"wrote {len(source_rows)} source rows through the catalog")
for row in source_rows:
    print(f"  {len(row['text']):>4} chars  url={row['url'] or '(none)':<32} {row['text'][:44]}...")

## Run the acquisition pipeline

Three nodes, three catalog writes — one per layer. Acquisition is a *separate*
pipeline from `index_build` on purpose: fetching is slow and rate-limited and should
happen once, while an index gets rebuilt many times over the same snapshot as
settings are tuned.

run_pipeline(
    "corpus_ingest",
    corpus={
        "field_map": {"text": "text", "url": "url"},
        "metadata_fields": ["label", "netloc"],
        "default_language": "en",
        "id_prefix": "demo",
        "min_text_chars": 32,
    },
    corpus_selection={"languages": None, "metadata_equals": None, "max_documents": None},
)
print("corpus_ingest complete")

## What each layer holds

Now read all three layers back **through the catalog**. This is the payoff of the
refactor: the layers are addressable by name, so you can inspect any stage without
knowing where it lives on disk.

raw = catalog.load("raw_corpus")
normalized = catalog.load("normalized_documents")
primary = catalog.load("documents")

print(f"01_raw           raw_corpus            {len(raw):>3} rows   (verbatim source)")
print(f"02_intermediate  normalized_documents  {len(normalized):>3} docs   (Document schema)")
print(f"03_primary       documents             {len(primary):>3} docs   (build-ready)")
print()
print(f"normalisation removed {len(raw) - len(normalized)} of {len(raw)} rows")

### Which rows were dropped, and why

The normaliser skips unusable rows rather than raising on them. That is a deliberate
choice: one malformed row out of 100,000 must not fail a multi-hour production build.
Here we reconstruct the reason for each drop.

from cybernaut_mini.corpus import CorpusSourceConfig, make_document_id

config = CorpusSourceConfig(
    field_map={"text": "text", "url": "url"},
    metadata_fields=["label", "netloc"],
    id_prefix="demo",
    min_text_chars=32,
)

kept_ids = {doc["id"] for doc in normalized}
seen: set[str] = set()

print(f"{'verdict':<12} {'reason':<22} url")
print("-" * 74)
for row in raw:
    text = " ".join(row["text"].split())
    natural_key = row["url"] or text
    doc_id = make_document_id(config.id_prefix, natural_key)

    if len(text) < config.min_text_chars:
        verdict, reason = "DROPPED", f"< {config.min_text_chars} chars"
    elif doc_id in seen:
        verdict, reason = "DROPPED", "duplicate natural key"
    else:
        verdict, reason = "kept", ""
        seen.add(doc_id)

    print(f"{verdict:<12} {reason:<22} {row['url'] or '(no url)'}")

print()
print(f"survivors: {len(kept_ids)}")

### Whitespace and derived titles

These corpora ship passages with no title, but the shard manifest, the shard summary,
and the `title\ntext` string that gets embedded all assume one exists. A title is
therefore derived from the first sentence, cut on a word boundary.

## Dynamic 1 — ids do not depend on row order

This is the property everything else rests on. Ids are `blake2b` hashes of the row's
natural key (its `url`, or the body text when there is none), **not** sequential
counters. Re-fetching a corpus whose rows came back in a different order therefore
produces the same ids, the same shard assignments, and the same byte-for-byte index.

Sequential ids would renumber every document and silently invalidate every stored
relevance judgment.

import random

from cybernaut_mini.corpus import normalize_rows

forward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(source_rows, config)]

shuffled = list(source_rows)
random.Random(0).shuffle(shuffled)
backward = [d.id for d in normalize_rows(shuffled, config)]

print("original order :", forward[:3], "...")
print("shuffled order :", backward[:3], "...")
print()
print("identical:", forward == backward)
assert forward == backward, "ids must not depend on row order"

## Dynamic 2 — `min_text_chars` trades size against quality

The knob that decides how much of a public corpus survives. Sweeping it shows the
cost directly: too low and boilerplate and navigation text become "documents" that
pollute every shard's keyword profile; too high and you discard real content.

print(f"{'min_text_chars':>15} {'documents kept':>16} {'mean text length':>18}")
print("-" * 52)
for threshold in (0, 16, 32, 80, 120, 400):
    swept = CorpusSourceConfig(
        field_map={"text": "text", "url": "url"},
        metadata_fields=["label", "netloc"],
        id_prefix="demo",
        min_text_chars=threshold,
    )
    docs = normalize_rows(source_rows, swept)
    mean_len = sum(len(d.text) for d in docs) / len(docs) if docs else 0.0
    print(f"{threshold:>15} {len(docs):>16} {mean_len:>18.1f}")

print()
print("conf/prod uses 120: long enough to exclude nav text and stubs from a web corpus.")

## Dynamic 3 — selection narrows without re-fetching

`select_documents` runs *after* normalisation, between the intermediate and primary
layers. That ordering matters: narrowing the corpus never requires downloading it
again, so you can re-scope a build for free.

from cybernaut_mini.pipelines.corpus_ingest.nodes import select_documents

print(f"{'selection':<44} {'documents':>10}")
print("-" * 56)
print(f"{'(no filter)':<44} {len(normalized):>10}")

for label, params in [
    ("languages=['en']", {"languages": ["en"]}),
    ("metadata_equals={'label': 'prediction'}", {"metadata_equals": {"label": "prediction"}}),
    ("max_documents=3", {"max_documents": 3}),
]:
    try:
        kept = select_documents(normalized, params)
        print(f"{label:<44} {len(kept):>10}")
    except ValueError as exc:
        print(f"{label:<44} {'ERROR':>10}  {exc}")

## Takeaways

| Observation | Consequence |
|---|---|
| Ids are content-derived, not positional | A re-fetch in a different order still rebuilds the identical index |
| Unusable rows are skipped, not raised on | One bad row in 100,000 cannot fail a multi-hour build |
| Selection sits after normalisation | Re-scoping a corpus costs zero network calls |
| Every read and write went through `catalog` | Swapping the local source for a pinned Hugging Face repo is a `conf/prod` edit, not a code change |

Next: [`02_shard_anatomy.ipynb`](02_shard_anatomy.ipynb) takes the corpus this
produced and asks whether the shards built from it are actually coherent.

"""Execute every notebook against the real catalog.

A notebook that is not executed is documentation that rots. These tests run each
notebook end to end in a fresh kernel, so a renamed catalog entry, a changed node
signature, or a removed helper fails the build instead of leaving a notebook that
quietly no longer works.

Network access is asserted off, not merely assumed off: the devcontainer injects .env,
so NOSIBLE_API_KEY is ambient and the API-reference notebook would otherwise fire real
billable requests on every run.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

nbformat = pytest.importorskip("nbformat")
nbclient = pytest.importorskip("nbclient")

REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
NOTEBOOK_DIR = REPO_ROOT / "notebooks"
NOTEBOOKS = sorted(NOTEBOOK_DIR.glob("*.ipynb"))

#: Guards against a notebook opening a path directly instead of going through the
#: catalog. These are the fixture paths a notebook is most likely to reach for.
_DIRECT_PATH_SMELLS = (
    'open("data/',
    "open('data/",
    'read_text("data/',
    'Path("data/sample',
    "Path('data/sample",
    'np.load("artifacts',
    'open("artifacts',
)


def test_notebooks_are_discovered() -> None:
    """Fail loudly if the glob stops matching — an empty suite must not look green."""
    assert NOTEBOOKS, f"no notebooks found in {NOTEBOOK_DIR}"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("notebook_path", NOTEBOOKS, ids=lambda p: p.stem)
def test_notebook_executes(notebook_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    """Run the notebook in a fresh kernel; any cell exception fails the test."""
    # Never make live API calls from a test run, even on a machine where a developer
    # has opted in for interactive use.
    monkeypatch.delenv("CYBERNAUT_LIVE_API", raising=False)

    notebook = nbformat.read(notebook_path, as_version=4)
    client = nbclient.NotebookClient(
        notebook,
        timeout=600,
        kernel_name="python3",
        # Catalog paths are relative to the project root.
        resources={"metadata": {"path": str(REPO_ROOT)}},
    )
    client.execute()

    errors = [
        output
        for cell in notebook.cells
        for output in cell.get("outputs", [])
        if output.get("output_type") == "error"
    ]
    assert not errors, (
        f"{notebook_path.name} raised {errors[0]['ename']}: {errors[0]['evalue']}\n"
        + "\n".join(errors[0].get("traceback", [])[-8:])
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("notebook_path", NOTEBOOKS, ids=lambda p: p.stem)
def test_notebook_has_a_mermaid_diagram(notebook_path: Path) -> None:
    """Every notebook is a teaching artifact, so it carries a diagram GitHub renders."""
    notebook = nbformat.read(notebook_path, as_version=4)
    markdown = "\n".join(
        "".join(cell["source"]) for cell in notebook.cells if cell["cell_type"] == "markdown"
    )
    assert "```mermaid" in markdown, f"{notebook_path.name} has no ```mermaid block"


@pytest.mark.parametrize("notebook_path", NOTEBOOKS, ids=lambda p: p.stem)
def test_notebook_reads_through_the_catalog(notebook_path: Path) -> None:
    """No notebook may open a data path directly — that is the drift this prevents."""
    notebook = nbformat.read(notebook_path, as_version=4)
    source = "\n".join(
        "".join(cell["source"]) for cell in notebook.cells if cell["cell_type"] == "code"
    )
    offenders = [smell for smell in _DIRECT_PATH_SMELLS if smell in source]
    assert not offenders, (
        f"{notebook_path.name} opens a data path directly ({offenders}); "
        f"load it via `catalog.load(...)` instead"
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("notebook_path", NOTEBOOKS, ids=lambda p: p.stem)
def test_notebook_is_committed_without_outputs(notebook_path: Path) -> None:
    """Outputs are regenerated on every run, so committing them only creates diff noise."""
    raw = json.loads(notebook_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    with_outputs = [
        cell.get("execution_count")
        for cell in raw["cells"]
        if cell.get("cell_type") == "code" and cell.get("outputs")
    ]
    assert not with_outputs, (
        f"{notebook_path.name} has stored outputs; clear them before committing "
        f"(the test suite regenerates them)"
    )


def test_every_notebook_is_listed_in_the_readme() -> None:
    """A notebook nobody can find is a notebook nobody maintains."""
    readme = NOTEBOOK_DIR / "README.md"
    assert readme.is_file(), "notebooks/README.md is missing"
    content = readme.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    missing = [path.name for path in NOTEBOOKS if path.name not in content]
    assert not missing, f"notebooks/README.md does not mention: {missing}"

def kedro_catalog(env: str = "local", **runtime_params: Any) -> Any:
    """Return the Kedro ``DataCatalog`` — the notebook's only data entry point.

    Every notebook loads through this rather than opening paths, so a renamed or
    repointed dataset surfaces as a failure in the notebook run instead of a
    notebook that quietly reads a stale file.
    """
    with kedro_session(env, **runtime_params) as session:
        return session.load_context().catalog


def run_pipeline(name: str, env: str = "local", **runtime_params: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Run a registered pipeline from a notebook and return its free outputs."""
    with kedro_session(env, **runtime_params) as session:
        result: dict[str, Any] = session.run(pipeline_name=name)
        return result


#: Settings that reproduce ``make build-fixture`` (configs/tiny.yaml): the hash
#: embedder, so a notebook never needs a model download or network access.
FIXTURE_BUILD_PARAMS: dict[str, Any] = {
    "input_path": "data/01_raw/fixtures/documents.jsonl",
    "index_path": "artifacts/fixture",
    "judgments_path": "data/01_raw/fixtures/judgments.jsonl",
    "embedding": {"provider": "hash", "dim": 256},
    "index": {
        "n_shards": 8,
        "max_keywords": 30,
        "max_entities": 30,
        "cooccurrence_window": 5,
        "min_edge_count": 2,
    },
    "seed": 42,
    "offline": True,
}


def ensure_fixture_index(index_path: str = "artifacts/fixture") -> Path:
    """Build the fixture index if it is absent, then return its path.

    ``_VALID`` is written last by the index writer, so its presence means a complete
    index and the build is skipped. That keeps a notebook run from overwriting an
    index the reader built themselves.
    """
    root = _bootstrap()
    target = root / index_path
    if (target / "_VALID").exists():
        return target

    params = dict(FIXTURE_BUILD_PARAMS)

    "| Unusable rows are skipped, not raised on | One bad row in 100,000 cannot fail a multi-hour build |\n"
    "| Two sources with different column schemas | `field_map` in `CorpusSourceConfig` handles translation; the normaliser never branches |\n"
    "| Merge deduplicates by id | A ccn- and mir- collision (impossible with disjoint prefixes) would silently keep the first occurrence |\n"
    "| Selection sits after the merge | Re-scoping a corpus costs zero network calls |\n"
    "| Every read and write went through `catalog` | Swapping a local source for a pinned Hugging Face repo is a `conf/prod` edit, not a code change |\n"
    "\n"
    "Next: [`02_shard_anatomy.ipynb`](02_shard_anatomy.ipynb) takes the corpus this\n"
    "produced and asks whether the shards built from it are actually coherent."
)

    if cell['cell_type'] == 'code':

When true: `load_dataset(..., streaming=True)` + `itertools.islice(dataset, max_rows)`; keep the SHA-pinning guards unchanged; implement the missing-column check for the streaming path via `dataset.features` (or first-row keys if features is None) so the same DatasetError fires. Add unit tests in tests/test_storage.py style with a mocked `datasets` module (see how existing tests mock; no network in tests): streaming slices stop at max_rows, column projection works, missing column raises, revision guards still fire. content.subject: M4.1: shard_recall@N metric + eval wiring
content.description: Implement shard_recall@N per Phase 2.1 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md: fraction of qrels-positive documents whose home shard is among the N shards the router selected (N = configured beam/select width). Add `shard_recall_at_n: float` to EvalMetrics (src/cybernaut_mini/evals.py:107) plus a pure function computing it (follow the style of recall_at_k at evals.py:75 — pure, docstringed with blog ref/assumptions/alternatives). Wire it into the evaluation pipeline (src/cybernaut_mini/pipelines/evaluation/nodes.py:49 evaluate_node and the report_node summary at nodes.py:94) with a per-mode breakdown; the retrieval call path must surface WHICH shards were selected per query — check src/cybernaut_mini/retrieval.py and routing.py for the shard-selection result and thread it through without changing public API defaults. Also thread the doc→shard mapping from the shard index (see ShardIndexDataset / src/cybernaut_mini/indexing.py). Add unit tests (tests/test_retrieval.py or a new tests/test_evals file consistent with existing naming) covering: perfect selection = 1.0, zero overlap = 0.0, partial, and empty-qrels guard. Run `uv run pytest -q` and `uv run ruff check .` + `uv run mypy src` before completing. Pull latest main first (Phase 0 lands before you start).

content.subject: M1.4: MIRACL qrels → Judgment loader + tests
content.description: Build the MIRACL en dev topics+qrels → Judgment loader per Phase 1.4 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md. Read .omc/research/m1-discovery.md FIRST for exact repo/config/column names and SHAs (task #2 produces it). Implementation: a pure normalization function (new module src/cybernaut_mini/pipelines/corpus_ingest/ or src/cybernaut_mini/corpus.py — follow where CorpusSourceConfig lives) mapping topic rows + qrels rows onto Judgment {query_id, question, relevant_document_ids: dict[str,int]} (src/cybernaut_mini/models.py:255), with docids prefixed to match the corpus id_prefix scheme ('mir') so judgment docids align with Document ids built by the ingest. Grades preserved (MIRACL is binary 0/1 — keep the int). Kedro wiring: catalog entries for the raw topics/qrels sources (HuggingFaceDataset, pinned SHAs from discovery doc) and an output JsonlDataset at data/03_primary/miracl_en_dev_judgments.jsonl in conf/prod/catalog.yml — coordinate with task #7 (prod conf rewrite) via team-lead if you both touch conf/prod at the same time; prefer putting ONLY the judgments entries in and messaging the lead. Every judgment docid must resolve against the corpus — add a validation guard that raises listing missing docids. Unit tests with in-memory rows (no network): mapping, prefixing, grade preservation, empty-qrels raise. Run `uv run pytest -q` + `uv run ruff check .` before completing.

content.subject: M1.3: multi-source corpus_ingest (ccnews + miracl branches + merge)
content.description: Extend corpus_ingest to two sources per Phase 1.3 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md. Read .omc/research/m1-discovery.md FIRST (task #2 output) for field maps. Current pipeline: snapshot_raw_corpus → normalize_corpus → select_documents (src/cybernaut_mini/pipelines/corpus_ingest/nodes.py, pipeline.py). Add a second source branch: catalog inputs raw_corpus_source (ccnews) and raw_corpus_source_miracl, each with its own snapshot + normalize (per-source CorpusSourceConfig from parameters: id_prefix 'ccn' / 'mir' so ids cannot collide), then a new pure `merge_documents` node (dedupe by id — raise on collision, deterministic order: sort by id) feeding the existing select_documents. Keep nodes pure (no I/O — sources come from the catalog, per the module docstring at nodes.py:1-27). Corpus composition rule from the plan: the miracl branch must NOT be capped (all qrels-referenced docs stay in); the ccnews branch takes the max_rows/max_documents cap so total lands ≈200k. Parameterize per-source selection in conf/base/parameters.yml (base keeps null/off defaults so the fixture path still works single-source; document that). Update conf/base/catalog.yml with the new intermediate entries (miracl paths). Unit tests for merge (collision raise, ordering, empty-branch raise) in tests/test_build.py style. Run `uv run pytest -q` + `uv run ruff check .` + `uv run mypy src` before completing. Follow the learning-first docstring convention (blog ref, assumptions, alternatives rejected).

content.subject: M1.6: prod conf rewrite — CC-News + MIRACL sources, 256 shards
content.description: Rewrite conf/prod per Phase 1.6 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md, replacing the NOSIBLE/prediction source (ruled out by scope Amendment #6). Keep the judgments entries task #5 adds — merge, don't clobber; message team-lead if you hit a conflict. conf/prod/parameters.yml: per-source corpus field_maps from the discovery doc (ccnews id_prefix 'ccn', miracl 'mir', min_text_chars per discovery recommendation), corpus_selection.languages [en], index.n_shards 256 with an updated rationale comment (200k docs / 256 shards ≈ 780 docs/shard — between the 390 the old comment argued and the scope target's 1000), embedding block unchanged (e5-small pinned revision stays). content.subject: M4.2-4.4: calibration + 200k build + eval + baseline doc
content.description: Per Phase 2.2-2.4 of .omc/plans/m1-m4-real-data-eval-baseline.md. All M1 tasks and shard_recall@N (#4) must be complete. (1) Calibration: run the production pipeline with max_rows≈20k (`scripts/with-accel.sh uv run kedro run --env prod --pipeline production --params ...` or a temporary max_rows override — do NOT edit the committed conf for this), record wall-clock; extrapolate to 200k and report the estimate to team-lead BEFORE starting the full run (lead decides go/no-go if extrapolation exceeds ~4h). (2) Full run: 200k docs / 256 shards with `scripts/with-accel.sh` (MPS + thread tuning), then `uv run kedro run --env prod --pipeline evaluation`. Record wall-clock + peak RSS (e.g. /usr/bin/time -l). (3) Verify acceptance criteria 2-4 of the plan: 256 shards present, doc count in [190k, 200k], every judgment docid resolves in the index, eval_report.json has 4 modes × 5 metrics incl. shard_recall@N with no all-zero/NaN mode. (4) Write docs/baselines/ccnews-miracl-200k.md: per-mode metric table, corpus SHAs, embedder revision (conf/prod/parameters.yml), shard count, build wall-clock, machine description; label metrics as MIRACL benchmark metrics never to be merged with generated per-shard evals (scope Amendment #7). (5) Sanity gates: hybrid must not underperform BOTH lexical and dense; shard_recall@N must beat random-N baseline (compute random baseline as N/256 expected).
